blocks.markdown: Insured deposits — objectives: define deposit and insured deposit (Sec. 5(g), (k)), apply the P1M MDIC and aggregation rules, distinguish the four exclusions, and use the splitting, fictitious-deposit, and remedy doctrines.

A **deposit** is money or its equivalent the BANK RECEIVED in the usual course of business — the receipt element is everything. An **insured deposit** is what a bona fide depositor is owed for legitimate deposits at closure, capped at the MDIC (**P1,000,000** since 15 March 2025). An **insured bank** is simply any bank whose deposits are insured under the charter.

Sec. 5(g) does three jobs at once: **defines deposit** (receipt + usual course + BSP-form evidence), **carves out offshore-payable obligations** (with a foreign-branch opt-in), and **lists the four never-payable accounts** — with PDIC's rulings final and executory, reviewable only by CA certiorari within 30 days.

Apply the receipt rule to two recurring patterns. **Pattern 1 — the money never arrived**: a branch manager issues a passbook but pockets the cash, or a funding check bounces and is never replaced. Result: no deposit, no insurance — the paper is worthless against PDIC however official it looks. **Pattern 2 — the money arrived but the product is not a deposit**: placements called 'deposits' that are really trust or investment products. Result: excluded as investments (substance over label). **Remember**: 'received by a bank' + 'usual course of business' + 'evidenced per BSP rules' — all three must concur, and PDIC checks them against the bank's own records.

Sec. 5(k) sets the **aggregation math** (same right and capacity; joint separate from individual; equal co-owner shares; juridical-person presumption; authenticity requirement) and the **MDIC machinery** (statutory P500,000 text + Board raise authority + 3-year review + systemic-threat lever).

Worked example (2026 closure, P1M MDIC): Rico has P1.2M individual savings plus a P1.6M 'and/or' account with wife Mira (equal-sharing document; Mira has nothing else). **Step 1** — individual: P1.2M capped at P1M → Rico gets P1M. **Step 2** — joint is SEPARATE: P1.6M split P800,000 each. **Step 3** — check each co-owner's joint aggregate against P1M: both pass. Payable: Rico P1.8M total, Mira P800,000. Variations to master: 'and' vs 'or' vs 'and/or' makes NO difference; a corporation-plus-officer joint account is presumed the corporation's entirely; every co-owner's joint interests ACROSS all joint accounts aggregate toward one maximum; and amounts above the maximum stay as uninsured claims with equal preference (Sec. 20).
The operative coverage rule today: **P1,000,000.00 per depositor per bank since 15 March 2025** — plus the decal and exact insurance-statement duties banks must display.

blocks.markdown: **Trap: P500,000 is history, not law, for new closures.** The statute still prints P500,000 because Sec. 5(k) states the figure while delegating increases to the Board — but the payable maximum since 15 March 2025 is P1M. In computation problems, first ask WHEN the bank closed: before 15 March 2025 → P500,000; on or after → P1,000,000. Stating P500,000 as 'current' is an error.

blocks.markdown: The IRR draws the working line: **fictitious = not real** (simulated, unfunded, or unrecorded); **fraudulent = knowingly schemed** (deceit, breach of trust, unconscientious advantage).

Two exclusion mechanics: the **five investment indicators** (no debtor-creditor link, trust/agency relation, at-risk principal, lock-up) and the **AML deferral rule** (freeze pending case → pay only on clearing judgment → never pay adjudged proceeds) — plus the **60-day verified reconsideration** lifeline on new evidence.

Splitting in one sentence: **over-maximum money, broken into 2+ non-owner accounts, within 120 days before a holiday or closure order, to multiply coverage** — punished by denial plus 6-12 years and/or P50,000-P10M fine on bank insiders.

When PDIC denies an insurance claim, the depositor's ladder has exactly two rungs. **Rung 1 — reconsideration**: verified request on NEW evidence with affidavits within 60 days from denial (IRR Rule III, Sec. 3(d)). **Rung 2 — certiorari**: Rule 65 petition to the COURT OF APPEALS within 30 days from denial notice, solely for excess of jurisdiction or grave abuse of discretion — because PDIC is a quasi-judicial agency whose Sec. 5(g) actions are final and executory (So; Chugani). There is no RTC rung: the RTC has no jurisdiction, and Sec. 27 voids any lower-court injunction against PDIC. **Remember**: 60-day reconsideration is administrative grace; 30-day CA certiorari is the judicial remedy — plead the right one.

**Exam point — the legitimacy test (Chugani): received, recorded, regular.** A deposit counts only if (1) the bank RECEIVED it in the usual course, (2) it is RECORDED in the bank's books, and (3) the account was opened per BSP/PDIC forms. Fail any leg and PDIC properly denies; attack the denial only by showing PDIC acted capriciously on the evidence — mere disagreement with its findings is not grave abuse.
